clue.text: Come into view in middle of field on combine

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on another sits above it, so comes first
the centre letter of the five-letter word field is taken

parts.note: to combine is to merge

explanation.surface: A farm scene: something appears in the middle of a field on a combine harvester.
explanation.walkthrough: 'combine' reads as the harvester noun but works as the verb meaning join.
explanation.definitionFit: To appear or come out into sight is a plain synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Mostly bent over low, start working seriously

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece sits over the second, so comes before it
most of the word, with its final letter dropped, is used

parts.note: something buckled has been bent out of shape
feeling low is feeling down

explanation.surface: Someone stooping low, nearly doubled over, is about to get going.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for applying oneself diligently to a task after slacking.

clue.text: What bookie offers eccentric punters, finally

parts.note: an eccentric person is odd

indicators.note: the closing letter of punters is used

explanation.surface: A bookmaker's prices tempt odd gamblers in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A betting shop quotes the prices, or ratios of stake to winnings, on each runner.

clue.text: Flower, small at this time, ahead of fall

indicators.note: says the earlier pieces come before the final one in the answer

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
at this time means now
a fall is a drop

explanation.surface: A tiny bloom is shown just before it falls.
explanation.definitionFit: A small white early-spring bloom, an example of a flower.

clue.text: Pudding choice no good

parts.note: a plum job is a choice one
duff is British slang for useless or no good

explanation.surface: A dessert option is judged a failure.
explanation.walkthrough: PLUM DUFF is a traditional British boiled suet pudding with raisins.
explanation.definitionFit: A specific steamed suet dessert, so an example of a pudding.

clue.text: Eat, though no starter included in held-up Christmas meal

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other
in a down clue, held up means read upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: Noel is Christmas

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: to munch is to eat

explanation.surface: Someone eats despite missing the first course of a delayed Christmas dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held-up' suits a down clue, where reading upwards turns the festive word backwards to LEON; 'Eat' is a verb but supplies its letters, not the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal word for the midday repast, a type of meal.

clue.text: Palmist maybe having mint meeting with cashier

parts.note: a mint is a fortune, a huge sum of money
a bank teller is a cashier

explanation.surface: A palm reader with loads of money meets a bank clerk.
explanation.definitionFit: A palm reader is one example of a person who predicts the future.

clue.text: Energetic type having lots back in party

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: signals the word for lots is read backwards

parts.note: lots means many

explanation.surface: A lively person has a great many friends back at the party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' gives YNAM, the reversal, which is wrapped by the party word.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, a forceful and tireless person, like a generator of power.

clue.text: Low, daughter's spirit

parts.note: to low is to make the sound of cattle, i.e. moo

explanation.surface: A daughter's spirits are low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' looks like an adjective about sadness but is the verb for a cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirit as in temper or frame of mind, a synonym.

clue.text: Hoodie, a dull sort

definitions.meaning: British slang for an obsessive, boring person, a nerd

explanation.surface: A hooded youth is dismissed as boring.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a hooded weatherproof jacket and, in British slang, a geeky obsessive.

clue.text: Material for panelling perhaps revolted golf club

parts.note: people who revolted rose up
a wood is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: Members of a golf club rebel over the clubhouse panelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark tropical hardwood used for veneers and fine panels.

clue.text: Food and drink: see bubbly with food brought back in, a fast food item

indicators.note: the pieces are put inside the other one

parts.note: cheer, as in good cheer, is an old word for food and drink

indicators.note: lively and fizzing, so the letters of see are stirred up

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: signals the slang word for food is read backwards

parts.note: grub is slang for food

explanation.surface: A busy menu list: provisions, champagne and food returned, all fast food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Food and drink' is one unit, the old sense of good cheer, not two separate items; 'bubbly' and 'brought back' work on the next two words, which then sit inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A grilled patty topped with a cheese slice in a bun, a staple of quick-service restaurants.

clue.text: Energy of outfit that's on with work

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece sits on top of the rest

parts.note: a getup is an outfit
and means with, together with
to go is to work or function

explanation.surface: Energy comes from clothing that is worn while at work.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for drive, enthusiasm and initiative.

clue.text: Introduce, on vessel, a pre-eminent performer

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: to start something is to introduce it
an urn is a vessel

explanation.surface: A star act is introduced aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship but is a container.
explanation.definitionFit: The headline act of a show, the most celebrated entertainer on the bill.

clue.text: Modest about page delivering something newsworthy

indicators.note: the word for modest goes around the other piece

parts.note: coy means modest or shy

explanation.surface: A shy person handles a page that brings news.
explanation.definitionFit: In journalism, material good enough to print is called good newspaper text.

clue.text: Sailors? Chay at sea, with rest floundering

indicators.note: confused, so the letters of Chay are muddled
struggling about, so the letters of rest are jumbled

explanation.surface: Chay Blyth, the yachtsman, adrift at sea while the others struggle.
explanation.walkthrough: Chay Blyth is a famous British round-the-world sailor; his name is anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who sail recreational craft are a kind of sailor, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Open no more, last in street

parts.note: something over is finished, no more

indicators.note: the closing letter of street is taken

explanation.surface: A shop at the end of the street is open no longer.
explanation.definitionFit: Open as in public and not concealed, a synonym of the adjective.

clue.text: Course in horsemanship at Hickstead

indicators.note: the letters lie within the run of words that follow

explanation.surface: A riding course at Hickstead, the West Sussex showjumping venue.
explanation.definitionFit: A track or route followed is a synonym for a course.

clue.text: Caught on, passing peer

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
something passing is fleeting, short-lived

explanation.surface: A passing nobleman catches on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peer' suggests a lord but means someone of the same age.
explanation.definitionFit: A person living at the same time or of the same age, i.e. an equal in age.

clue.text: Go round old gallery after little resistance shown

indicators.note: the later pieces follow the first

parts.note: R is the physics symbol for resistance
the Tate is a London art gallery

explanation.surface: Visitors tour an old gallery with little opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn or spin about an axis is a synonym.

clue.text: Fell on top of large jump

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: to fell a tree is to axe it
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Someone falls on top of a big jump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fell' reads as fall's past tense but is the verb to chop down.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure-skating leap with one and a half rotations.

clue.text: Former head admitting it in survey

parts.note: ex means former
the poll is the head

explanation.surface: An ex-headteacher owns up to something in a questionnaire.
explanation.definitionFit: A poll of voters leaving polling stations, a kind of survey.

clue.text: Swear-word used in boathouse

indicators.note: the letters are found inside the following word

explanation.surface: Bad language is heard in a boathouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swear-word' suggests a profanity, but means a solemn promise.
explanation.definitionFit: A sworn promise, a word one swears, as well as a curse.

clue.text: New set of books published, yet to be removed?

parts.note: OT, the Old Testament, is a set of books
a book that is out is published

explanation.surface: A new book set is published, still available.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batter still in at the end has not been dismissed.
explanation.definitionFit: The cricket phrase for a batter never dismissed, still at the crease.

clue.text: A wine in college at Cambridge before beginning of term

indicators.note: the college piece comes ahead of the next

parts.note: Clare is a Cambridge college

indicators.note: the opening letter of term is taken

explanation.surface: Wine served at a Cambridge college as term begins.
explanation.definitionFit: Red Bordeaux, so one particular wine.

clue.text: Equipment: a large amount is needed by one to make pasta

indicators.note: the earlier pieces are followed by the last

parts.note: a rig is equipment
a ton is a large amount
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Much equipment is needed by one person making pasta.
explanation.definitionFit: Ridged tube-shaped Italian noodles, a type of pasta.
